body: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. We propose Jacobian-causal memory control (JCMC), which represents each authorized memory intervention by a predicted influence signature in a shared behavioral measurement space, selects interventions against a target effect and side-effect budget, and compares predicted with observed effects before retaining or rolling back the intervention. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadratic local-approximation bound, characterize the target effects reachable by a set of signatures, bound selection regret under signature error, and bound non-additive interactions between simultaneous memories. The paper reports no benchmark measurements; it defines a paired counterfactual estimator and an evaluation protocol comparing JCMC with relevance, graph, and policy-filtered retrieval baselines. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if those simpler baselines match effect targeting, side-effect control, and rollback utility under equal model, memory, policy, and cost budgets.
summaryZh: 语言模型系统中持久记忆的雅可比因果记忆控制。持久记忆系统不仅选择检索哪些记录，还选择哪些先验信息可以改变当前的推理。我们提出雅可比因果记忆控制（JCMC），它通过共享行为测量空间中的预测影响签名来表示每个授权的记忆干预，根据目标效果和副作用预算选择干预措施，并在保留或回滚干预之前将预测与观察到的效果进行比较。
